correctness.rationale: The signed matrix-tree identity is proved directly by row multilinearity and acyclic functional-graph triangularization. Odd n gives odd coefficients; a recursively constructed skew ±1 matrix with ±1 row sums and determinant one supplies an attainable multiplier. Even n gives divisibility by 2^(n-2) through odd-entry row subtraction; cyclic regular-tournament signs give determinant exactly 2^(n-2) by a root-of-unity product. A rank-one determinant lemma gives a vanishing root-spoke sign assignment for all even n>=4; n=2 is checked separately. Both exact-arithmetic programs replay finite cases, without substituting experiments for infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The precise natural invariant is the smallest positive Fourier eigenvalue of the arborescence counting-convolution operator, which controls sharp Hilbert-space deconvolution stability. The result determines it in every dimension, proves the complete invertibility parity boundary and gives explicit sharp and null witnesses. It is not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical rank increment; the all-order arithmetic and circulant/skew constructions are the substantive contribution.
